Native R descriptive graphics for source-aligned eye-tracking diagnostics

etr_native_visual_diagnostics.Rd

Plots planar gaze paths, a selected functional principal component, a zero-based DTW alignment path, or descriptive rank agreement among distance specifications, without importing Python.

Usage

etr_plot_planar_trajectories(trajectories, max_curves = 40L,
  alpha = 0.35, invert_y = TRUE, ...)

etr_plot_fpca_component(result, component = 0L, dimension = NULL,
  sd_multiplier = 2, ...)

etr_plot_dynamic_time_warping_alignment(result, ...)

etr_plot_trajectory_distance_rank_correlations(result, ...)

Arguments

trajectories

Complete native trajectory set with two or more channels.

max_curves

Maximum number of curves; NULL selects all.

alpha

Plot line opacity in (0, 1].

invert_y

Reverse the screen-space vertical axis.

result

Native FPCA, DTW-with-path, or trajectory distance-sensitivity result, as appropriate.

component

Zero-based fitted FPCA component index.

dimension

Functional dimension, or NULL for the first fitted channel.

sd_multiplier

Positive score standard-deviation multiplier.

...

Additional base plotting options.

Value

The plotting function draws using base R graphics and invisibly returns auditable plot geometry: selected IDs and limits, the mean and SD curves, the zero-based DTW path, or the symmetric Spearman matrix.

Details

These are native-R scientific plot-geometry implementations aligned with public eyetrajectoriespy 1.2 names. Python plot functions return Matplotlib Axes objects whereas these functions draw on an R graphics device and return native R data invisibly. Therefore this is NOT exact Python output-object equivalence or a fully certified public source contract. The source-contract certification ledger remains independent.
